## Who this course is for

Social scientists who have used AI as a chatbot, mostly for text, and have never used Python or R. Seniority and field do not matter.

Two reactions are common.

*"This is for programmers."* It is not. You will not type a single command. You give instructions in plain language, as you would to a research assistant. Even Python is installed by the agent, which explains each step first.

*"I don't need this."* Maybe so. This course does not argue the point. It lets you find out on your own material, for the cost of an afternoon and one month of subscription. You stay the author: nothing changes without your approval.

We use one tool: **Claude Code, in the Claude desktop app**, on Windows, Mac or Linux. Similar agents exist, and what you learn carries over. While learning, one tool is enough.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What is an AI agent?

**A chatbot** is a conversation in a browser. You paste text or upload a file, it answers, and you copy the answer back. It knows only what you gave it in that conversation.

**An agent** is the same AI model with three additions. First, access to **one folder** on your computer that you choose. Second, the ability to **act** there: open files, write and run small programs, save files. Third, a **loop**: it takes a step, looks at the result, and decides the next one, until the task is done or it needs you.

The loop makes the difference. Ask for *"a chart of turnout by age group from survey.csv"*. A chatbot needs the file uploaded and may guess what the columns mean. The agent:

1. opens the file and sees that age is called `age_cat`, not `age`;
2. writes a short program and runs it;
3. hits an error because some ages are coded "refused", and asks you how to handle them;
4. runs it again, opens the chart to check it, and saves it in `output/`.

You see every step, and at first it asks your permission before each one.

Think of a very fast research assistant at your computer: well read, new to your project, and sometimes confidently wrong. Your job shifts from doing each step to **deciding, instructing and checking**. Checking becomes the most important part.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What you need

- **A paid Claude plan.** Claude Code needs **Claude Pro** or higher (about \$20/month, cancel any time; [pricing](https://claude.com/pricing)). A university Claude Team or Enterprise plan also works.
- **A computer** with Windows 10/11, macOS, or Linux (Ubuntu or Debian).
- **Permission to install software.** University laptops may need IT approval. Try first; ask if blocked.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The course

Three hands-on parts, about an hour each, and a live demo. If something fails, nothing is broken: check the troubleshooting table, or ask the agent what went wrong.

## A short glossary

- **Agent:** an AI model that acts on your computer (reads files, runs code, saves results) in a loop until a task is done.
- **Harness:** a word you will hear later: the program around the model that gives it these abilities. Claude Code is one.
- **Session:** one conversation with the agent. Each starts fresh.
- **Context window:** what the model can see at once. Long sessions fill it up, and quality drops.
- **Terminal:** a text window for typing commands. The agent uses one behind the scenes; you don't have to.
- **Environment (Python):** a project's own copy of Python and its packages, kept in the `.venv` folder.
- **Markdown (`.md`):** plain text with a few formatting symbols. The common language of people and agents.
- **`AGENTS.md`:** standing instructions the agent reads at the start of every session.
- **Skill:** a recipe file the agent follows for one type of task.
